title: Elon Musk's 5 most noteworthy comments during SpaceX's first earnings call
excerpt: Elon Musk said that SpaceX engineers building data centers was like the New York Yankees playing a Little League team.
content_html:
By Theron Mohamed

You're currently following this author! Want to unfollow? Unsubscribe via the link in your email.

Elon Musk issued a jaw-dropping revenue forecast, ridiculed the ease of building data centers compared to rockets, and envisioned factories on the Moon during SpaceX's first earnings call on Tuesday.

The Tesla and SpaceX CEO — who is well-known for his grandiose predictions — also touted Starlink's potential for global domination, and predicted AI will become dramatically more advanced by the end of next year.

Here are Musk's five most interesting comments during SpaceX's inaugural earnings call after its blockbuster market debut in June.

1. Rocketing revenue

Musk told Wall Street analysts that SpaceX's internal projections have it reaching $1 trillion in revenue in 2030, instead of 2031 as it had forecast before its IPO. He also said there's a "nonzero chance of that being in 2029."

To put that in perspective, Walmart and Amazon, which generate more revenue than any other public companies, reported net sales of $706 billion and $717 billion, respectively, in their last full financial years.

SpaceX generated $12.5 billion in first-half revenue, a 54% increase from the same period in 2025.

From fully autonomous vehicles to the first crewed mission to Mars, Musk has a long history of setting ambitious timelines for milestones, only to fail to meet them.

He acknowledged back in 2018 that he's "typically optimistic" about when things will occur, but added that what he predicts "pretty much always happens, but not exactly on the timeframe."

2. Data centers vs. rockets

Musk said that building data centers "ain't rocket science," whereas building rockets is extremely challenging because they "desperately want to blow themselves into tiny pieces."

He quipped that tasking rocket engineers to construct data centers was "kind of ridiculous, frankly," and represented a "trivial problem" for them.

Musk quipped that it was like the "New York Yankees going in and playing a Little League team."

Big Tech companies, including Microsoft, Meta, Amazon, Alphabet, and Oracle, are pouring hundreds of billions of dollars into building data centers to power the AI revolution.

The immense demand for microchips, power, and water has strained supply chains and pressured energy grids and reservoirs.

3. Linking up the world

Musk said it's "not out of the question" that Starlink will eventually deliver a "majority of the world's internet, at least in countries where we're allowed to operate, which is the vast majority of countries."

In another example of his famously optimistic timelines, Musk added that it won't be in the "infinity future" but rather in "less than 10 years."

Starlink, the satellite-communications arm of SpaceX, has emerged as a key provider of internet to planes, ships, and far-flung locales.

However, it has yet to meaningfully disrupt the core urban broadband businesses of established internet providers such as T-Mobile and Verizon.

4. Mission to the Moon

Musk predicted that SpaceX will build "factories on the Moon," and "robots will be helpful with that."

He acknowledged that "sounds like super sci-fi right now," adding it might seem "totally nuts" but "you can probably scale to 1,000 times the economy of Earth in terms of intelligence launched into space, but probably maybe even 1 million times."

5. Getting smarter

Musk hailed the launch of Claude 4.5 last September as "one of the milestones and a credit to Anthropic."

He said it was a "shock to the system" how good the AI model was.

Musk pointed to the immense progress in AI over the past two years, saying models from two summers ago feel like they "should be in a museum."

Based on recent rates of improvement, Musk said that by the end of next year, it's "not clear to me that there's anything that — digital at least — that AI won't be able to do."

作者：Theron Mohamed 您目前正在关注该作者！ 想要取消关注吗？ 通过电子邮件中的链接取消订阅。

埃隆·马斯克 (Elon Musk) 在周二 SpaceX 的第一次财报电话会议上发布了令人瞠目结舌的收入预测，嘲笑了与火箭相比建造数据中心的容易程度，并设想在月球上建工厂。

这位特斯拉和 SpaceX 的首席执行官——以其宏伟的预测而闻名——也吹捧了星链统治全球的潜力，并预测到明年年底人工智能将变得更加先进。

以下是 SpaceX 在 6 月份轰动市场后的首次财报电话会议上，马斯克发表的五条最有趣的言论。

1. 收入猛增

马斯克告诉华尔街分析师，SpaceX 的内部预测是 2030 年收入达到 1 万亿美元，而不是 IPO 前预测的 2031 年。 他还表示“2029 年出现这种情况的可能性非零”。

从这个角度来看，沃尔玛和亚马逊的收入比任何其他上市公司都多，在上一个完整财年的净销售额分别为 7060 亿美元和 7170 亿美元。

SpaceX 上半年营收 125 亿美元，较 2025 年同期增长 54%。

从全自动驾驶汽车到首次载人火星任务，马斯克长期以来一直为里程碑设定雄心勃勃的时间表，但最终未能实现。

他早在 2018 年就承认，他对事情何时发生“通常持乐观态度”，但补充说，他预测的事情“几乎总是会发生，但并不完全在时间表上”。

2. 数据中心与火箭

马斯克表示，建设数据中心“不是火箭科学”，而建造火箭则极具挑战性，因为它们“迫切希望将自己炸成碎片”。

他打趣道，让火箭工程师建造数据中心的任务“坦白说有点荒谬”，对他们来说只是一个“微不足道的问题”。

马斯克打趣道，这就像“纽约洋基队进入并与一支少年棒球联盟球队比赛”。

微软、Meta、亚马逊、Alphabet 和甲骨文等大型科技公司正在投入数千亿美元建设数据中心，以推动人工智能革命。

对微芯片、电力和水的巨大需求给供应链带来了压力，也给电网和水库带来了压力。

3. 连接世界

马斯克表示，星链最终将提供“世界上大部分互联网，至少在我们被允许运营的国家，也就是绝大多数国家”，“并非不可能”。

在他著名的乐观时间表的另一个例子中，马斯克补充说，这不会发生在“无限的未来”，而是“不到 10 年”。

Starlink 是 SpaceX 的卫星通信部门，已成为飞机、船舶和偏远地区互联网的主要提供商。

然而，它尚未对 T-Mobile 和 Verizon 等老牌互联网提供商的核心城市宽带业务产生重大影响。

4. 月球任务

马斯克预测 SpaceX 将在“月球上建造工厂”，而“机器人将对此提供帮助”。

他承认这“现在听起来像超级科幻小说”，并补充说这可能看起来“完全疯狂”，但“就发射到太空的智能而言，你的经济规模可能是地球的 1000 倍，甚至可能是 100 万倍。”

5. 变得更聪明

马斯克称赞去年 9 月 Claude 4.5 的推出是“里程碑之一，也是对 Anthropic 的赞扬”。

他表示，人工智能模型的出色表现“让整个系统感到震惊”。

马斯克指出了过去两年人工智能取得的巨大进步，并表示两年前夏天的模型感觉“应该放在博物馆里”。

马斯克表示，根据最近的改进速度，到明年年底，“我不清楚是否有什么事情——至少是数字化的——人工智能无法做到。”
